Since the strophic line 935 διατομαῖς οὐ φίλαις [with hostile cuttings] does not correspond to it, Hermann wrote ἀχθέων [of griefs] in the antistrophe, and this indeed correctly, but the emendation of the preceding word, whether in the strophe or antistrophe, is uncertain. Hermann changed διατομαῖς [cuttings] to διαρταμαῖς [tearings], a word not read elsewhere, while Schütz, keeping διατομαῖς [cuttings] in the antistrophe, wrote διοδότων [given by Zeus], which, since it provides the most fitting metrical form, is perhaps to be considered true, although no other examples of this form are found except the not uncommon proper name Διόδοτος [Diodotus].
Thus Porson for διὸς νότῳ γᾶν εἰ [Zeus's... to the south wind... earth...].
